scenarios.name: replace-nvm-with-locked-mise-setup
scenarios.rationale: A hits every rubric item in order: brew install, `mise use node@22 python@3.12`, `mise lock`, committing both files, teammates running `mise install --locked`, removing nvm lines and adding the activate line. B uses `mise use --pin`, which departs from the stated command, and tells teammates to run plain `mise install` (the rubric also accepts that); it also covers the rest, but adds unnecessary caveats and a speculative `lockfile = true` setting.

scenarios.name: mise-toml-with-env-and-dependent-tasks
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: [tools], [env], a lint task, a test task with depends = ["lint"] and a run array, `mise run test`, `mise tasks ls`, and a note that node = "24" tracks the newest 24.x. A uses run with task references instead of depends, so it misses the key depends/run-array structure. It also never says that "24" is not an exact pin.

scenarios.name: ci-reproducible-with-lockfile-and-trust
scenarios.rationale: A covers the rubric closely: mise lock, committing mise.toml and mise.lock, install --locked, mise run, re-running lock on a missing entry, the untrusted-code warning, review before trust, and the note that mise run loads env and installs tools; B uses mise exec instead of mise run and never gives install --locked or the fix for a missing entry, though its trust warning is thorough.
